name: Calendar Skills
description: Prefer the calendar connector tools over driving the Calendar app UI.
instructions:
Never automate a calendar app's UI to view or manage events — use the dedicated tools instead, which read/write calendar accounts directly:
1. list_calendar_events supports date ranges and text search, and shows reminders and attendees per event.
2. create_calendar_event supports all_day, calendar_name (to pick a specific account like 'Work'), attendees (real invites on a synced Google calendar), and recurrence (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly with recurrence_count or recurrence_until).
3. edit_calendar_event updates only the fields you provide; get the event_id from list_calendar_events first.
4. delete_calendar_event always asks the user to confirm before removing anything — irreversible.

Choosing a source: list_calendar_events and create_calendar_event default to source='device' (the phone's own calendar accounts) and that is almost always right. Only pass source='google' or source='microsoft' when the user asks about an account that is not synced to this phone, or when the device calendar clearly does not contain what they described.

Event ids differ by source: device events have bare numeric ids, connector events are prefixed 'gcal:' or 'ms:'. edit_calendar_event and delete_calendar_event work on device ids only — for a connector event, tell the user it must be changed in that account's own app.

For 'am I free', 'when can we meet', or scheduling around existing commitments, use check_availability rather than listing events and reasoning about the gaps yourself. It needs a connected Google (with Calendar) or Microsoft account; if none is connected, fall back to list_calendar_events and say you are reading the device calendar only.

Only fall back to UI automation (open_app + navigate_app) for things these tools can't do, e.g. the app's own settings.
